    tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai¶

    IA generativa self-hosted: geração de texto, embeddings, VLM, moderação, cache, métricas e router.

    « IA e visão computacional

    A superfície de topo do genai — geração de texto, embeddings, VLM, moderação, cache, métricas e router. Os submódulos que exigem outra disciplina (hub, image, inventory, rag, audio) têm página própria.

    genai ¶

    Self-hosted generative AI — run HuggingFace models on your own hardware.

    The first slice ships the capacity check: before you download and load a model, ask whether the host can actually run it. Everything here imports without the [genai] extra; torch / transformers are only needed to probe real GPUs and (later) run inference.

    ANTHROPIC_STOP_REASONS module-attribute ¶

    ANTHROPIC_STOP_REASONS: dict[str, StopReason] = {
    "end_turn": "end",
    "stop_sequence": "end",
    "max_tokens": "max_tokens",
    "refusal": "refusal",
    "tool_use": "tool_use",
}

    Messages API stop_reason values to the normalized :data:StopReason.

    From the stop-reason table of https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages (end_turn, max_tokens, stop_sequence, tool_use, pause_turn, refusal). pause_turn and any value added later map to other.

    ANTHROPIC_VERSION module-attribute ¶

    ANTHROPIC_VERSION: str = '2023-06-01'

    The anthropic-version header value.

    The example value of the required header at https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/overview.

    DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS: int = 16000

    max_tokens sent when the call sets no max_new_tokens.

    The Messages API requires max_tokens on every request (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages), unlike the OpenAI and Ollama formats, where it is optional.

    DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_MODEL: str = 'claude-opus-5-5'

    The model used when none is given.

    The current Opus model id on the models table (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview) when this was written. Pass model to choose another; model ids are never guessed from a date.

    DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_URL module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_ANTHROPIC_URL: str = 'https://api.anthropic.com'

    API root; requests go to {base_url}/v1/messages.

    From https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/overview.

    DEFAULT_DEEPSEEK_MODEL module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_DEEPSEEK_MODEL: str = 'deepseek-flash'

    DeepSeek's default model id.

    The model field of https://api-docs.deepseek.com/api/create-chat-completion accepts deepseek-flash or deepseek-v4-pro when this was written.

    DEFAULT_DEEPSEEK_URL module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_DEEPSEEK_URL: str = 'https://api.deepseek.com'

    DeepSeek's OpenAI-format API root.

    From https://api-docs.deepseek.com/, which posts to https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions.

    DEFAULT_DOCUMENT_FILENAME module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_DOCUMENT_FILENAME: Final[str] = 'document.pdf'

    The filename :func:document_part sends when the caller gives none.

    Every base64 example of the OpenAI PDF guide passes a filename next to file_data, so the part always carries one.

    DEFAULT_GOOGLE_OPENAI_URL module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_GOOGLE_OPENAI_URL: Final[str] = (
    "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai"
)

    Gemini's OpenAI-compatible API root; /chat/completions is appended.

    From https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai, whose base_url is https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/. Stored without the trailing slash because the generator joins /chat/completions itself.

    DEFAULT_OPENAI_URL module-attribute ¶

    DEFAULT_OPENAI_URL: str = 'https://api.openai.com/v1'

    Where the wire format originates; override for any other provider.

    The servers entry of the official OpenAPI document (https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi).

    DOCUMENT_MEDIA_TYPES module-attribute ¶

    DOCUMENT_MEDIA_TYPES: Final[frozenset[str]] = frozenset({PDF_MEDIA_TYPE})

    Media types :func:document_part accepts.

    Only PDF. The OpenAI PDF guide (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/pdf-files) says Chat Completions "supports only .pdf (application/pdf)" for file_data, and the base64 document source of the Anthropic PDF guide (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/pdf-support) is application/pdf. Plain text goes in a text part instead.

    DOCUMENT_PROVIDERS module-attribute ¶

    DOCUMENT_PROVIDERS: Final[frozenset[HostedProvider]] = frozenset(
    {"anthropic", "openai"}
)

    Hosted providers whose documentation describes PDF input.

    Read on 2026-11-04:

    • anthropic — document blocks with a base64 application/pdf source (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/pdf-support).
    • openai — "Chat Completions accepts only PDF files as file content parts", with file_data as a data:application/pdf;base64,... URL (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/pdf-files).

    Left out, because their documentation does not describe it:

    • google — the OpenAI-compatibility page (https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai, which redirects to https://aistudio.google.com/docs/openai) documents image (image_url) and audio (input_audio) parts, and no file part.
    • deepseek — the chat-completion reference (https://api-docs.deepseek.com/api/create-chat-completion) lists a file part, but describes file_data as "a base64-encoded data URL of the image" and names no PDF or document format.

    The SDK's tests pin the request built for each provider, not a provider's answer: membership here is what the documentation says, not a live call.

    OPENAI_FINISH_REASONS module-attribute ¶

    OPENAI_FINISH_REASONS: dict[str, StopReason] = {
    "stop": "end",
    "length": "max_tokens",
    "content_filter": "refusal",
    "tool_calls": "tool_use",
}

    choices[].finish_reason values to the normalized :data:StopReason.

    The values documented for finish_reason in the official OpenAPI document (https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi, openapi.yaml): stop for a natural stop or a stop sequence, length for the token budget, content_filter for content omitted by a filter, tool_calls for a tool call. Anything else (the deprecated function_call, a provider's own value) maps to other.

    OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS_FIELD module-attribute ¶

    OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS_FIELD: Final[str] = 'max_completion_tokens'

    Where the output budget goes on OpenAI.

    The official OpenAPI document (https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi, branch main) marks max_tokens deprecated in favor of max_completion_tokens. The same value HostedGenAISettings.openai_kwargs() selects.

    PDF_MEDIA_TYPE module-attribute ¶

    PDF_MEDIA_TYPE: Final[str] = 'application/pdf'

    The media type of a PDF, the default of :func:document_part.

    StopReason module-attribute ¶

    StopReason = Literal['end', 'max_tokens', 'refusal', 'tool_use', 'other']

    Why a call stopped, normalized across providers.

    end is a natural stop (Anthropic end_turn / stop_sequence, OpenAI stop); max_tokens is a reply cut at the budget (max_tokens / length); refusal is a declined request (Anthropic refusal, OpenAI content_filter or a non-null message.refusal); tool_use is a tool call; other is anything the mapping does not name — the raw value is kept in :attr:StructuredCompletion.provider_stop_reason.

    StreamModeration module-attribute ¶

    StreamModeration = Literal['incremental', 'buffered']

    How :meth:AIChatPipeline.stream screens the reply when a moderator is set.

    • "incremental" — every piece is checked (together with everything generated before it) before it is sent; the first flagged check stops the stream and sends blocked_message. Pieces already sent stay sent.
    • "buffered" — the whole reply is generated and checked first, then sent as a single piece; nothing reaches the client before the verdict.

    StructuredOutputMode module-attribute ¶

    StructuredOutputMode = Literal['json_schema', 'json_object']

    How :meth:OpenAICompatGenerator.chat_structured asks for JSON.

    "json_schema" sends the schema as response_format (the ResponseFormatJsonSchema of the OpenAI spec). "json_object" asks only for some JSON object and states the schema in a system turn — for a provider whose response_format has no json_schema type, like DeepSeek (https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/json_mode).

    TRANSCRIPTION_RESPONSE_FORMAT module-attribute ¶

    TRANSCRIPTION_RESPONSE_FORMAT: str = 'verbose_json'

    The response_format every transcription asks for.

    verbose_json is the one format of the OpenAI spec whose body carries duration, language and segments; json carries only text.

    ThinkLevel module-attribute ¶

    ThinkLevel = bool | Literal['low', 'medium', 'high']

    The Ollama think field: on/off, or a reasoning level.

    Sent at the top level of /api/chat and /api/generate (inside options the daemon ignores it). True/False switch reasoning on or off on a model with the thinking capability; "low"/"medium"/ "high" pick a level on the models that support levels (gpt-oss).

    AIChatPipeline ¶

    AIChatPipeline(
    generator: TextBackend,
    *,
    memory: ChatMemory | PgChatMemory | None = None,
    web_search: WebSearch | None = None,
    tts: TextToSpeech | None = None,
    tools: list[Tool] | None = None,
    base_system_prompt: str = "",
    max_tool_iterations: int = 5,
    tokenizer: Any = None,
    max_context_tokens: int | None = None,
    moderator: ModerationBackend | None = None,
    blocked_message: str = "Sorry, I can't help with that request.",
    stream_moderation: StreamModeration = "incremental",
    parse_text_tool_calls: bool = True,
)

    Compose a text backend with memory, web search, TTS and tools.

    The pipeline owns no persistence and no model lifecycle — you inject ready objects and it orchestrates them per turn. Only the pieces you provide are wired: pass just a generator and you get plain chat; add a memory and every turn recalls + indexes; add tools and (when the backend supports chat_with_tools) a bounded tool loop runs.

    Example:

    >>> pipeline = AIChatPipeline(
...     OllamaGenerator("llama3.2"),
...     memory=chat_memory,
...     web_search=web_search,
... )
>>> result = await pipeline.respond(
...     user_id="u1", chat_id="c1", content="What is PIX?",
... )
>>> result.reply

    Tools available to the model (may be empty).

    System prompt prepended to every turn.

    Upper bound on tool-loop rounds.
    parse_text_tool_calls bool

    Whether a tool call written as JSON in the reply text is run like a native one.

    		 None

    stream_moderation StreamModeration

    How :meth:stream screens the reply — "incremental" (default) checks the accumulated text before sending each piece, so pieces keep flowing but a flagged reply is cut where it tripped; "buffered" checks the whole reply before sending anything, trading streaming for zero leakage. Ignored without a moderator.

    		 'incremental'
    parse_text_tool_calls bool

    When a tool-loop reply has no native tool_calls, read its text as a call: one JSON object {"name", "arguments"} (or a list of them), optionally in a single markdown fence, whose name is a registered tool. Some models choose the right tool and arguments but write the call in content; without this the JSON becomes the reply. Turn it off when a legitimate reply can be a JSON object whose name matches a tool name.

    		 True

    stream async ¶

    stream(
    *,
    user_id: str | UUID | None,
    chat_id: str | UUID,
    content: str,
    history: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
    images: list[str] | None = None,
    use_web_search: bool = False,
) -> AsyncIterator[str]

    Stream a reply piece by piece for a single chat turn.

    Runs the same recall + augment + (non-streamed) tool loop as :meth:respond to resolve any tool calls, then streams the final answer. Because :meth:TextBackend.stream takes a single prompt, the built message list is flattened into one prompt string (system + turns) — streaming is prompt-mode, and it does not itself stream the intermediate tool-call steps. The final answer is indexed into memory after the stream completes (best-effort).

    With a moderator, the input and history are screened first (a flagged input yields only blocked_message), and the reply is screened per stream_moderation:

    • "incremental" — before each piece is yielded, the text generated so far, including that piece, is checked. The first flagged check stops generation and yields blocked_message as the last piece. Pieces yielded before it cannot be recalled: the client keeps them. What the check guarantees is that the piece which makes the text flaggable is never sent — with :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.RuleModerator, a block-listed term is never emitted whole, though a prefix of it may be.
    • "buffered" — the reply is generated in full and checked once; the client receives either the whole reply as one piece or blocked_message, and nothing before the verdict.

    A blocked reply is not indexed into memory, matching :meth:respond.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    user_id str | UUID | None

    Owner of the conversation; None skips memory recall and indexing.

    		 required
    chat_id str | UUID

    The active chat.

    		 required
    content str

    The user's message.

    		 required
    history list[dict[str, Any]] | None

    Prior turns.

    		 None
    images list[str] | None

    Base64 images (placed on the user message; note prompt-mode streaming may not honor them for every backend).

    		 None
    use_web_search bool

    Augment the prompt with web context.

    		 False

    Yields:

    Name Type Description

    Text pieces of the reply as the backend produces them, or
    AsyncIterator[str]

    Example:

    >>> store = AIUsageStore(db, model=UsageModel, price_input_per_1k=0.00014)
>>> text, usage = await gen.generate_with_usage(prompt)
>>> await store.record(subject_id=user.id, service="summary", usage=usage)

    		 0.0
    price_output_per_1k float

    Cost of 1000 generated tokens.

    		 0.0
    price_cache_hit_per_1k float | None

    Cost of 1000 prompt tokens served from a cached prefix, when the provider bills those cheaper. None — the default — means "no separate cached rate", and prices the cached slice at price_input_per_1k like every other prompt token.

    None rather than 0.0 on purpose: 0.0 is a price, and defaulting to it would make an unconfigured store report cached tokens as free, understating every discounted call. An unconfigured price should never move a number.

    		 None

    estimate_cost ¶

    estimate_cost(
    input_tokens: int, output_tokens: int, *, cache_hit_tokens: int = 0
) -> float | None

    Price a set of token counts.

    Deliberately not stored on the row: a price correction then applies to the whole history at once, instead of leaving old rows priced with a number nobody remembers setting.

    Not rounded. Any fixed precision is wrong at some scale here: token prices live around 0.0001 per 1000, so rounding to cents reports zero for almost every single call, and even six decimals zeroes a one-token call — while a monthly total wants cents. The library therefore returns the number and leaves formatting to the boundary, which knows whether it is showing one call or a month.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    input_tokens int

    Prompt tokens, cached ones included — that is how providers report the field, so subtracting them here would double-discount.

    		 required
    output_tokens int

    Generated tokens.

    		 required
    cache_hit_tokens int

    How many of input_tokens came from a cached prefix. Priced at price_cache_hit_per_1k when one is configured; otherwise it changes nothing. Clamped to input_tokens: a provider reporting more cached tokens than prompt tokens is nonsense, and letting it through would produce a negative full-rate term.

    		 0

    Type Description
    float | None

    float | None

    configured — which the interface should read as "do not show a

    AudioGenerationConfig ¶

    Bases: BaseSchema

    Typed parameters for local text-to-audio generation.

    Passed to :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.AudioGenerator. Only the fields you set reach the pipeline, so a partial config layers on top of the model's own defaults. Those differ a lot: read from diffusers 0.39, AudioLDMPipeline defaults to 10 steps and guidance 2.5, MusicLDMPipeline to 200 steps and guidance 2.0.

    Example:

    >>> cfg = AudioGenerationConfig(seconds=10.0, steps=50, seed=0)
>>> clips = await generator.generate("rain on a tin roof", config=cfg)

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    negative_prompt str | None

    What to steer the sound away from.
    seconds float | None

    Length of each clip, at most 120.
    steps int | None

    Denoising steps, at most 1000.
    guidance_scale float | None

    How hard to follow the prompt.
    seed int | None

    RNG seed, 0 to 2**64 - 1 -- the range torch.manual_seed accepts (2**64 raised ValueError: Overflow when unpacking long long on torch 2.14). Set it and the same prompt gives the same waveform on the same hardware.
    num_waveforms int

    Clips per call, at most 8. These ceilings are the schema's absolute bounds; make_genai_router enforces tighter per-request limits from :class:GenAIRequestLimits on top.

    to_pipeline_kwargs ¶

    to_pipeline_kwargs() -> dict[str, Any]

    Return the explicitly-set pipeline keywords, in diffusers names.

    seed is excluded (it binds a torch.Generator), and seconds / steps / num_waveforms become audio_length_in_s / num_inference_steps / num_waveforms_per_prompt.

    Returns:

    Type Description
    dict[str, Any]

    dict[str, Any]: Keywords to splat into the pipeline call.

    BaseAIUsageModel ¶

    Bases: BaseModel

    Abstract usage table — one row per recorded AI call.

    Inherits id / is_active / created_at / updated_at from :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.db.model.BaseModel, so created_at is when the call happened and is what every aggregation buckets on.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    subject_id UUID | None

    Who the call is billed to — a user, a tenant, whatever the application charges. None for calls with no owner (a scheduled sweep, a system prompt), which is why the aggregations treat it as a real bucket rather than dropping it.
    service str | None

    Which capability spent it ("summary", "suggest_tasks"). None marks a row that carries duration instead of tokens, so the two never contaminate each other's sums.
    model str | None

    Which model answered, so a price change or a model swap stays attributable afterwards.
    input_tokens int

    Prompt tokens, as the provider reported them.
    output_tokens int

    Generated tokens.
    total_tokens int

    What the provider counts for the call — carried rather than summed, because cached-prefix discounts make the two disagree.
    duration_seconds float | None

    Wall-clock, for local inference that has no token bill.
    cache_hit_tokens int | None

    The slice of input_tokens the provider served from a cached prefix and billed cheaper — a subset, not an addition. Nullable rather than defaulted to zero on the column, because rows written before this column existed genuinely do not know their split, and claiming zero for them would price a discounted call at full rate.

    BatchScheduler ¶

    BatchScheduler(
    handler: Callable[[list[ItemT]], Awaitable[list[ResultT]]],
    *,
    max_batch: int = 32,
    max_wait_ms: float = 10.0,
)

    Bases: Generic[ItemT, ResultT]

    Merge concurrent :meth:submit calls into batched handler calls.

    A background loop drains a queue, forming a batch once either max_batch items are waiting or max_wait seconds have elapsed since the first queued item, then calls handler(batch) once and hands each caller its matching result by position.

    The handler is awaited, so it must be a coroutine function taking the whole batch. :meth:Embedder.embed is that shape already; its private _embed_many is not — it is synchronous, and awaiting it raises TypeError: object list can't be used in 'await' expression.

    Example:

    >>> async def embed_batch(texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
...     return await embedder.embed(texts)
>>> sched = BatchScheduler(embed_batch, max_batch=32, max_wait_ms=10)
>>> vec = await sched.submit("hello")   # coalesced with concurrent calls
>>> await sched.aclose()

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    max_batch int

    Max items per handler call.
    max_wait float

    Max seconds to wait forming a batch.

    Initialize the scheduler.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    handler Callable[[list[ItemT]], Awaitable[list[ResultT]]]

    Async batch function. Must return one output per input, in order.

    		 required
    max_batch int

    Max items per batch.

    		 32
    max_wait_ms float

    Max milliseconds to wait for a batch to fill before flushing what's queued.

    		 10.0

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    When max_batch is not positive.

    The verdict of whether the host can run a given model.

    When the memory of device could not be measured (memory_measured=False, e.g. CPU on macOS without psutil), the verdict is unknown rather than negative: fits is False because nothing was verified, available_bytes and headroom_pct are 0 and carry no information, and reason/suggestion say what to install to measure it.

    Whether the model is expected to fit on device. Only True when the free memory was measured and covers the estimate.

    The precision the estimate assumes.
    estimated_bytes int

    Estimated memory the model needs (weights + inference overhead).
    available_bytes int

    Memory available on device; 0 when memory_measured is False.
    headroom_pct float

    (available - estimated) / available * 100; negative when it doesn't fit, 0.0 when memory_measured is False.
    reason str

    Human-readable explanation of the verdict.
    suggestion str | None

    A concrete next step when it doesn't fit (e.g. quantize, offload to CPU) or when the memory could not be measured, or None when it fits.
    memory_measured bool

    Whether the free memory of device was read. False means the report is a "could not check", not a "does not fit".

    ClassifierModerator ¶

    ClassifierModerator(
    model_id: str,
    *,
    flagged_labels: list[str] | None = None,
    threshold: float = 0.5,
    device: str = "auto",
    cache_dir: str | None = None,
    hf_token: str | None = None,
    revision: str | None = None,
    local_files_only: bool | None = None,
    trust_remote_code: bool = False,
    idle_unload_seconds: float | None = None,
    hardware: HardwareInfo | None = None,
    activation: _Activation = "auto",
    window_tokens: int | None = 64,
    window_overlap: int = 16,
)

    A local text-classification moderator over transformers.

    Runs a sequence-classification model (e.g. a toxicity classifier), maps its labels via the model config, and flags the text when a configured label's score crosses threshold. Lazy-loaded; inference runs in a worker thread. Best-effort — validate the model on your language before relying on it. Needs the [genai] extra.

    Scores come from a sigmoid per label when the model is multi-label (config.problem_type == "multi_label_classification", as in unitary/toxic-bert) or has a single output, and from a softmax otherwise; activation= forces either. A softmax over independent labels splits the mass between them, so a text that is both toxic and insulting can score under the threshold on both.

    Text is never truncated: it is cut into short overlapping windows (64 tokens by default), every window is classified, and each label keeps its highest score across windows — so content placed after a long harmless prefix is still screened. The windows are short on purpose: a classifier such as unitary/toxic-bert dilutes one toxic sentence inside a few hundred benign tokens below the threshold, so a window as wide as the model's context (512) still lets that sentence through. Cost grows with the number of windows.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    model_id str

    The HuggingFace classifier id.
    threshold float

    Score above which a label flags the text.
    activation str

    "auto", "sigmoid" or "softmax".
    window_tokens int | None

    Tokens per window, special tokens included; None uses the model's whole context.
    window_overlap int

    Tokens shared by consecutive windows.

    Configure the moderator (does not load weights yet).

    observe_inventory ¶

    observe_inventory(report: ModelRuntimeReport) -> None

    Publish a runtime inventory as gauge values.

    Counters answer "how much work went through"; these answer "what is resident now", which is the question that explains an OOM. Feed it from a periodic task:

    >>> metrics.observe_inventory(registry.inventory(probe=False))

    The labelled gauges are cleared first, because they describe a snapshot: a model that unloaded between two calls must stop being reported, and an unlabelled leftover would read as still resident. Cleared-then-empty is the correct picture for a service holding nothing.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    report ModelRuntimeReport

    A :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.ModelRuntimeReport.

    GenAIRequestLimits ¶

    Bases: BaseSchema

    Per-request ceilings :func:make_genai_router enforces.

    Every GenAI endpoint turns request size into GPU time or memory: a 2 MB prompt with max_new_tokens=10**9, a 100 000-item /embed batch or a 100 000 x 100 000 image are each a way for one caller to hold the worker. The router checks the request against these limits before calling the model and answers 422 with the offending field and its limit in details. The defaults suit a small self-hosted deployment; pass your own instance to raise or lower any of them.

    max_new_tokens caps only the value a caller sends. A request that leaves it unset falls through to the generator's own default, which the operator — not the caller — chose.

    Example:

    >>> limits = GenAIRequestLimits(max_prompt_chars=8_000, max_top_k=20)
>>> router = make_genai_router(text_generator=gen, limits=limits)

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    max_prompt_chars int

    Largest prompt, in characters. Applies to the /generate prompt, the sum of every /chat message, the /rag query, each /embed text and the /image prompt and negative prompt.
    max_chat_messages int

    Most messages one /chat request may carry.
    max_new_tokens int

    Largest config.max_new_tokens accepted.
    max_embed_texts int

    Most texts one /embed request may carry.
    max_top_k int

    Largest top_k accepted by /rag.
    max_tts_chars int

    Largest /tts text, in characters.
    max_image_side int

    Largest config.width / config.height accepted by /image, in pixels.
    max_image_steps int

    Largest config.steps accepted by /image.
    max_audio_seconds float

    Largest config.seconds accepted by /audio.
    max_audio_steps int

    Largest config.steps accepted by /audio. The default admits MusicLDM's own default of 200.
    max_upload_bytes int

    Largest /transcribe upload, in bytes. The default equals DEFAULT_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES (25 MiB), the ceiling make_voice_router uses.

    GeneratedImage ¶

    Bases: BaseSchema

    One rendered image plus what it takes to render it again.

    The seed travels with the image on purpose. Diffusion is deterministic given a seed, so returning the seed the run actually used is the difference between "nice image, gone forever" and "nice image, here is how to get it back" — and when the caller passes no seed, only the generator knows which one was drawn.

    GenerationConfig ¶

    Bases: BaseSchema

    Typed generation parameters for the local text generators.

    Passed to :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.TextGenerator and :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.VisionTextGenerator, which apply every field the same way (tests/genai/test_vision_text_config.py fails when a field reaches one and not the other). Replaces loose **kwargs at the call site with a validated, self-describing, reusable object — build one config and pass it to generate / chat / stream. Only the fields you set are forwarded to model.generate (unset fields fall through to the generator's own defaults), so a partial config layers cleanly on top.

    Example:

    >>> cfg = GenerationConfig(max_new_tokens=512, temperature=0.2)
>>> await gen.generate("Explain PIX.", config=cfg)

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    max_new_tokens int | None

    Maximum tokens to generate (> 0).
    temperature float | None

    Sampling temperature (0..2); lower is more deterministic.
    top_p float | None

    Nucleus sampling probability mass (0..1).
    top_k int | None

    Top-k sampling cutoff (>= 0); 0 disables.
    repetition_penalty float | None

    Penalty for repeated tokens (> 0, 1.0 = no penalty).
    do_sample bool | None

    Sample (True) or use greedy decoding (False).
    seed int | None

    RNG seed for reproducible sampling.
    stop list[str]

    Stop strings that end generation early.

    to_generate_kwargs ¶

    to_generate_kwargs() -> dict[str, Any]

    Return only the set fields as model.generate keyword args.

    seed and stop are dropped from the mapping — they are not transformers generate kwargs. Both generators reapply them themselves: seed through a per-call torch.Generator and stop via the stop_strings generation argument (see :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.text._resolve_control).

    Returns:

    Type Description
    dict[str, Any]

    dict[str, Any]: The explicitly-set generation kwargs.

    GenerationStoppedError ¶

    Bases: RuntimeError

    Raised when a generation was stopped through its stop_event.

    Local generation runs in a worker thread, and a thread cannot be cancelled from outside — so cancelling the awaiting coroutine leaves the GPU producing tokens for a reply nobody will read. The stop_event is how the decision reaches the thread, and this is what the thread raises once it has honoured it: the work stopped because it was told to, not because it went wrong.

    HardwareInfo ¶

    Bases: BaseSchema

    A snapshot of the host's compute resources.

    A byte field that could not be read stays 0 so arithmetic on it keeps working, and its *_measured flag turns False: read the flag before treating 0 as "nothing free". Both flags default to True, so a snapshot built by hand (tests, a cached probe) means what its numbers say.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    cpu_cores int

    Logical CPU cores.
    ram_total_bytes int

    Total RAM this process can use: the host's, or the cgroup memory limit when ram_cgroup_limited is True; 0 when ram_measured is False.
    ram_available_bytes int

    Currently available RAM, bounded by the cgroup when ram_cgroup_limited is True; 0 when ram_measured is False.
    ram_measured bool

    Whether the two RAM fields were read. :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.probe_hardware sets it to False when neither psutil (the [metrics] extra) nor, on Linux, /proc/meminfo could be read — in practice, Windows or macOS without psutil.
    ram_cgroup_limited bool

    Whether the RAM fields come from a Linux cgroup memory limit (a container's --memory) that is below the host's RAM, rather than from the host. Defaults to False.
    has_cuda bool

    Whether a CUDA GPU is usable via torch.
    gpus list[GPUInfo]

    Per-CUDA-device memory (empty without CUDA).
    has_mps bool

    Whether Apple Metal (MPS) is available.
    disk_free_bytes int

    Free space on the model cache filesystem; 0 when disk_measured is False.
    disk_measured bool

    Whether disk_free_bytes was read. False when the filesystem query raised OSError (e.g. the directory does not exist).
    warnings list[str]

    Environment problems the probe detected that will make a later model load fail, each a sentence that names the cause and the fix. Empty when nothing was detected, which is not a guarantee that every load succeeds. Today the only one is a CUDA 13 torch next to ctranslate2 (faster-whisper), whose wheels link against CUDA 12.

    ImageGenerationConfig ¶

    Bases: BaseSchema

    Typed parameters for local image generation.

    Passed to :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.ImageGenerator. Only the fields you set are forwarded to the diffusion pipeline, so a partial config layers on top of the model's own defaults — which matters here more than for text, because the right step count and guidance scale differ by an order of magnitude between a distilled turbo model and a full SDXL.

    Example:

    >>> cfg = ImageGenerationConfig(steps=4, guidance_scale=0.0, seed=7)
>>> images = await generator.generate("a red bicycle", config=cfg)

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description

    ModelDtypeEnum ¶

    Bases: BaseStrEnum

    Weight precision a model is loaded in.

    Fewer bytes per parameter → smaller memory footprint, at some quality cost. int8 / int4 require quantization (the [genai-quant] extra).

    • FLOAT32 — 4 bytes/param (full precision).
    • FLOAT16 / BFLOAT16 — 2 bytes/param (the usual GPU default).
    • INT8 — 1 byte/param (quantized).
    • INT4 — ~0.5 byte/param (quantized).

    ModelRef ¶

    Bases: BaseSchema

    Everything needed to resolve one set of weights, reproducibly.

    A bare model id names a moving target: the author pushes to main and the next restart loads different weights. Pinning revision to a commit sha (see :func:resolve_revision) makes a deployment reproducible and removes a supply-chain surface — the weights a service runs stop depending on when it happened to boot.

    Example:

    >>> ref = ModelRef(
...     model_id="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
...     revision="a8b602d",
...     local_files_only=True,
... )
>>> ref.loader_kwargs()
{'revision': 'a8b602d', 'local_files_only': True}

    Name Type Description

    The Hub model id ("org/name") or a local path.

    Branch, tag or commit sha. None means the Hub default (main) — convenient, not reproducible.
    cache_dir str | None

    Where weights are cached. None takes GENAI_CACHE_DIR from the environment, falling back to the HF_HUB_CACHE default.
    token str | None

    Hub token for gated or private repositories. None takes GENAI_HF_TOKEN.

    When True, never touch the network: load from the cache or fail — what an air-gapped or deploy-frozen production host wants. None takes GENAI_OFFLINE, falling back to False.
    trust_remote_code bool

    When True, allow the repository's own Python to run at load time. Some architectures require it; it also executes code you did not review, so it stays opt-in and per-model.

    ModelRegistry ¶

    ModelRegistry(max_models: int = 2)

    An LRU cache of loaded models keyed by a string id.

    Each held object must expose unload() (TextGenerator and Embedder do), called on eviction.

    Eviction never frees weights under a running call: the SDK loaders defer an unload() that arrives while calls are in flight until the last one finishes.

    A handle kept after its eviction (model = registry.get(...) at startup, used for every request) does not reload behind the registry. Its next call re-registers it under its key — replacing whatever object a later :meth:get built there — and evicts the least-recently-used entry to make room, then waits for that entry's in-flight calls to finish before building. So max_models keeps holding for SDK loaders however the handle was obtained.

    The same wait applies to a model :meth:get just built: when the entry it pushed out still has calls running, the new model's first call blocks until they finish, so the two are never resident together. One allowance remains — a call made from inside another model's call does not wait, since the outer call could be what the evicted model is waiting on; there the ceiling is exceeded until that outer call ends. A third-party object exposing only unload() has no hook for any of this; hold those through :meth:get per request.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    max_models int

    How many models may be live at once before the least-recently-used is evicted.

    Initialize the registry.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    max_models int

    unload_idle ¶

    unload_idle() -> list[str]

    Free every held model that has sat idle past its own threshold.

    Entries stay in the registry — a TextGenerator that unloaded its weights is still the right object to hand out, and it reloads on next use. This frees memory without losing the configuration, so it is what a periodic task should call; :meth:evict and :meth:evict_all are for forgetting the entry entirely.

    A handle that does not implement unload_if_idle is skipped: without an idle clock there is no basis to decide, and unloading someone's model on a guess is worse than leaving it.

    Returns:

    Type Description
    list[str]

    list[str]: The keys whose models this call unloaded.

    A reference clip (path or bytes) whose melody the music follows; only a musicgen-melody checkpoint takes one. It is decoded with :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.audio.load_audio (a 16-bit WAV needs nothing else; other formats need PyAV, from [genai-audio]), mixed to mono at the model's rate, and its input features are cast to the model's precision -- in bf16 they otherwise fail with mat1 and mat2 must have the same dtype. A string is always a path, never fetched; a missing file is refused before the model loads, and a clip longer than :data:MAX_MELODY_SECONDS is refused when decoded.

    		 None

    list[GeneratedAudio]

    list[GeneratedAudio]

    num_waveforms above 1 they differ, so reproducing clip i
    list[GeneratedAudio]

    takes the same seed, the same num_waveforms and index i.

    Reproducibility holds while nothing else draws from torch's process-wide RNG during the render: keep max_concurrent=1 and do not run other torch sampling in the same process concurrently.

    Bases: OllamaError

    The prompt does not fit the context window and truncate was False.

    By default the daemon cuts an overflowing prompt to about half the window and answers 200. With truncate=False it refuses instead: 400 with an exceed_context_size_error that carries the prompt size and the window (reproduced on Ollama 0.30.11 on /api/chat and /api/generate, streamed or not, before any line is streamed). Raise num_ctx or shorten the prompt.

    OllamaError ¶

    OllamaError(model: str, detail: str)

    Bases: RuntimeError

    The Ollama daemon answered with an {"error": ...} body.

    The daemon reports some failures (model not pulled, out of memory, a runner crash mid-stream) as a JSON object with an error key — on a 200 response or as one line of an NDJSON stream. Treating that object as a normal reply yields an empty completion, or a stream that ends as if it had finished. This exception surfaces it instead.

    OllamaFormatIgnoredError ¶

    OllamaFormatIgnoredError(model: str, content: str, think: ThinkLevel | None)

    Bases: OllamaError, ValueError

    A structured call came back as free text instead of the JSON asked for.

    The request carried the schema as format and the reply holds no JSON object, so the daemon did not constrain the decoder. Reproduced on Ollama 0.30.11: ornith:35b with think=false answered **Nome:** Ana Costa ... with 200 in 3 of 3 calls, while the same request with think omitted or true returned the object 3 of 3. ornith-1.5:9b, gpt-oss:20b and ministral-3:14b honoured format with think=false (3 of 3 each).

    Subclasses ValueError, which is what a reply without a JSON object raised before, so code already catching that keeps working.

    Bases: _OllamaRequestMixin

    Text generation backed by an Ollama daemon.

    A drop-in alternative to :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.text.TextGenerator: it exposes the same generate / chat / stream surface (so it slots into :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.make_genai_router) but delegates inference to Ollama over HTTP. No torch, no local weights, no load() — the daemon must be running and the model pulled.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    model str

    The Ollama model tag.
    base_url str

    The daemon base URL.
    config GenerationConfig | None

    Default generation parameters, layered under every call's own.
    options dict[str, Any]

    Raw Ollama options sent with every request, num_ctx included when set.
    think ThinkLevel | None

    Default top-level think field, or None to send none.
    truncate bool | None

    Default top-level truncate field, or None to send none.

    Configure the daemon connection and the per-request defaults.

    The connection arguments are the ones every Ollama client takes; the last three exist because some callers pass no options at all. The :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.agents.Agent loop calls chat_with_tools(messages, tools) and nothing else, so before these a generator driving an agent always ran on the daemon's defaults — including its context window, which truncates the prompt silently. Measured on Ollama 0.30.11 with lfm2.5-thinking:1.2b: a 35,018-token chat came back with prompt_eval_count 2,051 and no error under the default, and 35,018 with num_ctx=65536. An agent's prompt is the system turn, every tool spec and every tool result so far, so it reaches that ceiling within a few steps.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model str

    The Ollama model tag (must already be pulled).

    		 required

    		 DEFAULT_OLLAMA_URL

    		 120.0
    keep_alive str | float | None

    		 None

    An injected client; one is created lazily and owned by this instance when None.

    		 None
    transport AsyncBaseTransport | None

    Transport for the lazily-created client (tests). Ignored with http_client.

    		 None
    retry_policy RetryPolicy | None

    Retry configuration for the lazily-created client. None keeps the HTTPClient defaults but does not retry a read timeout: the daemon aborts the generation when the client gives up, so a retry redoes it from zero and the failure would arrive after three timeouts instead of one. Ignored with http_client.

    		 None
    metrics GenAIMetrics | None

    Optional Prometheus metrics.

    		 None
    generation_cache GenerationCache | AsyncGenerationCache | None

    Optional prompt→completion cache for deterministic calls.

    		 None
    config GenerationConfig | None

    Default generation parameters for every call. A call's own config is layered over it field by field, and its keyword overrides win over both.

    		 None
    num_ctx int | None

    Context window in tokens, sent as the num_ctx option on every request. None leaves the daemon's default (4096 without OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH). Either way, a reply whose prompt_eval_count shows the daemon truncated the prompt logs a WARNING on the tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.ollama logger.

    		 None
    options dict[str, Any] | None

    Raw Ollama options sent on every request (num_thread, num_gpu, …), under the ones a call's config or overrides produce.

    		 None
    think ThinkLevel | None

    Default think field for every request, sent at the top level of the body (inside options the daemon ignores it). None sends nothing and leaves the model's default; a call's own think wins over it. Measured in the 2026-11-26/27 local-LLM study (Ollama 0.30.11, temperature 0): gpt-oss:20b with "low" solved 97.1% of 34 tool tasks at p50 1.44 s, against 94.1% at 1.68 s for its default (medium) and 97.1% at 3.59 s for "high"; ornith-1.5:9b with False scored 93.3 per field on 33 extraction cases at p50 1.34 s, against 95.0 at 5.60 s with True.

    		 None
    truncate bool | None

    Default truncate field for every request, sent at the top level of the body. False makes a prompt longer than the context window fail with :class:OllamaContextExceededError instead of being cut to about half the window; True is the daemon's own default (measured on Ollama 0.30.11: the same prompt_eval_count as omitting it). None sends nothing; a call's own truncate wins over it.

    		 None

    chat_structured async ¶

    chat_structured(
    messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
    schema: type[StructuredT],
    *,
    config: GenerationConfig | None = None,
    think: ThinkLevel | None = None,
    truncate: bool | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> StructuredT

    Generate a chat reply constrained to a Pydantic schema.

    The messages list is what makes a system instruction separable from the payload being read. That separation helps, but it is the smaller half of the story: the first thing a long document needs is a context window that fits it. Ollama defaults num_ctx to 4096 tokens and truncates the rest silently, and under truncation both shapes degrade — the concatenated one worse, because the instruction competes for room with the document. Measured over a 24,086-character document with 20 extractable items, three runs each: at num_ctx=4096 the system turn returned 0, 6 and 5 items against 1 and 2 (and one empty reply) concatenated; at num_ctx=16384 both returned all 20, every run. Size the window first, then keep the instruction in its own turn.

    format is posted at the top level of the request body, which is where the daemon reads it. Sending it inside options — what happens when a schema is passed as a keyword to :meth:chat — is ignored silently: the call returns 200 with free text, and the caller finds out at validation time, or worse, at a parse that happens to succeed.

    As in :meth:generate_structured, the posted schema lists every property in required at every level; optional fields stay nullable and the reply is validated against schema itself.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    messages list[dict[str, Any]]

    Chat turns, each {"role": ..., "content": ...}. Put the instruction in a system turn and the content being read in user.

    		 required
    schema type[StructuredT]

    The Pydantic model to produce.

    		 required
    config GenerationConfig | None

    Typed generation parameters.

    		 None
    think ThinkLevel | None

    Top-level think for this call; None uses the generator's default. False makes some models ignore format (see :class:OllamaFormatIgnoredError).

    		 None
    truncate bool | None

    Top-level truncate for this call; None uses the generator's default.

    		 None
    **kwargs Any

    Per-call generation overrides (win over config).

    		 {}

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    StructuredT StructuredT

    The validated instance.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    TypeError

    When format is passed as a keyword — the schema argument is what sets it, and a keyword would be dropped into options and ignored.
    OllamaFormatIgnoredError

    When the reply holds no JSON object, so the daemon did not apply the format constraint.
    OllamaThinkingUnsupportedError

    When think is set and the model has no thinking capability.
    OllamaContextExceededError

    When truncate is False and the prompt does not fit the context window.
    ValidationError

    When the JSON fails schema validation.
    Example 
    from pydantic import BaseModel

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import OllamaGenerator


class Invoice(BaseModel):
    number: str
    total_cents: int


async def read(document: str) -> Invoice:
    "Extract the invoice fields from a document."
    generator = OllamaGenerator(model="gpt-oss:20b")
    return await generator.chat_structured(
        [
            {"role": "system", "content": "Extract the invoice fields."},
            {"role": "user", "content": document},
        ],
        Invoice,
    )

    generate_structured async ¶

    generate_structured(
    prompt: str,
    schema: type[StructuredT],
    *,
    system: str | None = None,
    config: GenerationConfig | None = None,
    think: ThinkLevel | None = None,
    truncate: bool | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> StructuredT

    Generate a completion constrained to a Pydantic schema.

    Passes the schema as the Ollama format field (the daemon enforces JSON-schema-valid output natively) and parses the reply into an instance of schema. No [genai-structured] extra needed — the constraint lives in the daemon. The posted schema lists every property in required at every level, defaulted ones included, so the model cannot skip a field and let its default stand in for the answer; optional fields stay nullable.

    The request goes to /api/chat, not /api/generate. That is not a style choice: on a harmony/reasoning model such as gpt-oss, /api/generate with a format constraint answers 200 OK with a non-zero eval_count and an empty response — the reply lands in a reasoning channel the endpoint does not surface. Measured against gpt-oss:20b: /api/generate without format works, /api/generate with format returns empty, /api/chat with format returns the JSON in message.content. Non-reasoning models behave the same on either endpoint, so /api/chat is correct for both.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    prompt str

    The input text. With a schema in hand the model does not need to be told to answer as JSON — the daemon constrains the decoder.

    		 required
    schema type[StructuredT]

    The Pydantic model to produce.

    		 required
    system str | None

    Instruction sent as its own system turn ahead of prompt. Prefer it over prefixing the instruction to a long document: a several-thousand-token prompt buries an instruction placed above it, and the model answers about the document while ignoring the ask.

    		 None
    config GenerationConfig | None

    Typed generation parameters.

    		 None
    think ThinkLevel | None

    Top-level think for this call; None uses the generator's default. False makes some models ignore format (see :class:OllamaFormatIgnoredError).

    		 None
    truncate bool | None

    Top-level truncate for this call; None uses the generator's default.

    Bases: _OllamaClientMixin

    Text-to-speech and speech-to-text backed by an Ollama daemon.

    Pull the model first (ollama pull phonon for English speech, ollama pull lfm3-audio for 18 languages and transcription). A request the daemon refuses with 400 (a model without the speech or audio capability, an unknown voice, bad input) raises :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.exceptions.ValidationException with the daemon's message; a model that is not pulled, or a daemon failure, raises :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.OllamaError. It satisfies :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.audio.SpeechTranscriber and :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.audio.SpeechSynthesizer, so it backs /transcribe and /tts in :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.make_genai_router.

    keep_alive, metrics and generation_cache from the shared Ollama client stay None: the speech endpoints ignore keep_alive, and there is no text generation to meter or cache.

    speech_response async ¶

    speech_response(
    text: str,
    /,
    *,
    voice: str | None = None,
    speaker: str | None = None,
    language: str | None = None,
    response_format: SpeechFormat = "pcm",
) -> StreamingResponse

    Return a StreamingResponse that fails as 422 when it should.

    A StreamingResponse sends its status and headers before reading the first chunk, so an error raised by :meth:stream_speech on its first chunk (an unknown voice) reaches the client as 200 with an empty body, and Starlette logs Caught handled exception, but response already started -- measured. This method pulls the first chunk before building the response: a refusal raises here, where :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.register_exception_handlers turns it into the SDK's 422, and the audio that follows still streams.

    stream_speech async ¶

    stream_speech(
    text: str,
    /,
    *,
    voice: str | None = None,
    speaker: str | None = None,
    language: str | None = None,
    response_format: SpeechFormat = "pcm",
) -> AsyncGenerator[bytes, None]

    Yield the speech audio as the daemon generates it.

    Where :meth:synthesize waits for the whole clip, this yields each chunk as the daemon flushes it, so a player (or a StreamingResponse) starts before synthesis ends. "pcm" (the default here) is raw 16-bit mono 24 kHz with no header, the format a streaming player wants; "wav" starts with a header whose sizes are the streamed 0xFFFFFFFF placeholder, since the length is not known up front.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    text str

    The text to speak.

    		 required
    voice str | None

    A voice name from :meth:voices.

    		 None
    speaker str | None

    The same as voice.

    		 None
    language str | None

    Must stay None; the voice decides the language.

    		 None
    response_format SpeechFormat

    "pcm" or "wav".

    		 'pcm'

    Closing the iterator early (a client that disconnects from a StreamingResponse) closes the daemon connection right away. There is no tracing span here, unlike :meth:synthesize: a span held across yield is closed by whoever finalizes the generator, and a consumer that breaks out of the loop without closing it leaves that to the event loop, in another context -- measured with OpenTelemetry installed, every such stream logged Failed to detach context. A "wav" stream is passed through as the daemon sends it; only :meth:synthesize, which holds the whole clip, can rewrite the header sizes.

    Yields:

    Name Type Description
    bytes AsyncGenerator[bytes, None]

    The audio, chunk by chunk.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValidationException

    Before any request when language is given or voice and speaker disagree; before the first chunk when the daemon refuses with 400.
    OllamaError

    When the model is not pulled or the daemon fails.
    HTTPError

    When the daemon cannot be reached or does not answer in time.

    Torch-free text embedder over ONNX Runtime.

    Example:

    >>> from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import OnnxEmbedder
>>> emb = OnnxEmbedder(
...     "model.onnx",
...     tokenizer="sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2",
...     normalize=True,
... )
>>> vectors = await emb.embed(["hello", "world"])

    pooling Literal['mean', 'cls']

    "mean" or "cls".
    idle_unload_seconds float | None

    Idle threshold for :meth:unload_if_idle.

    Configure the embedder (does not load the model yet).

    The ONNX graph is already on local disk, so only the tokenizer can come from the Hub — the pinning keywords apply to it alone. tokenizers.Tokenizer.from_pretrained accepts revision and token and nothing else, so there is no offline flag to forward here; point tokenizer at a local tokenizer.json when the host must not reach the network.

Match the model card; ignored when the graph already outputs a pooled (batch, dim) embedding.

    chat_structured async ¶

    chat_structured(
    messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
    schema: type[StructuredT],
    *,
    config: GenerationConfig | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> StructuredT

    Generate a reply constrained to a Pydantic schema.

    With structured_output="json_schema" the schema goes out as response_format ({"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name", "schema"}}), named after the model class. strict is left at the spec's default (false): strict mode accepts only a subset of JSON Schema, and a Pydantic model with defaults can fall outside it. With "json_object" the provider is asked for a JSON object and the schema is stated in a trailing system turn — DeepSeek's JSON mode requires the word "json" in the prompt (https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/json_mode). Either way the reply is validated here against schema.

    RedisEmbeddingCache(
    redis: Redis, *, prefix: str = "genai:emb:", ttl_seconds: int | None = None
)

    A Redis-backed embedding cache shared across workers/processes.

    Vectors are stored as JSON under "<prefix><key>". Satisfies :class:AsyncEmbeddingCache, so it drops into :class:Embedder exactly where :class:InMemoryEmbeddingCache goes — the difference is that every worker hits the same store, so a vector computed by one request is reused by the next, on any worker.

    Example:

    >>> from redis.asyncio import Redis
>>> cache = RedisEmbeddingCache(Redis.from_url("redis://localhost"))
>>> emb = Embedder("sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2", cache=cache)

    RuleModerator ¶

    RuleModerator(blocklist: list[str], *, category: str = 'blocked')

    A dependency-free block-list moderator.

    Flags text containing any block-listed term as a whole word, case-insensitively. Before matching, both the terms and the text are NFKC-normalized, stripped of format characters (zero-width and bidi controls) and casefolded, so a zero-width space (U+200B) inside the word or its fullwidth spelling (U+FF53 U+FF45 ...) still hits "secret". Whole-word means "not glued to a word character on either side" (lookarounds, not \b), which is what makes terms that start or end with punctuation — "$hit", "c++" — match at all. Predictable and fast — the deterministic default when a classifier's quality (especially in PT-BR) can't be trusted. Homoglyphs from other scripts (Cyrillic U+0435 standing in for Latin "e") are not folded; list those spellings explicitly.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    category str

    The category label reported on a match.

    Initialize the moderator.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    blocklist list[str]

    Terms that flag the text (whole-word, case-insensitive, normalized as described on the class). Terms that normalize to an empty string are ignored.

    		 required
    category str

    The category label reported on a match.

    		 'blocked'

    A lazily-loaded local causal LM with streaming and idle unload.

    Example:

    >>> gen = TextGenerator("Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", quantization="int4")
>>> await gen.generate("Explain PIX in one sentence.")
>>> async for token in gen.stream("..."):
...     ...
>>> gen.unload()   # free VRAM

Point it at a mounted volume when the process is a container, so the layer does not re-download the model on every restart.

    Branch, tag or commit sha to load. None follows the Hub default, which moves when the author pushes; pin a sha (see :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.resolve_revision) for a reproducible deployment.

    Load from the cache without touching the network — what an air-gapped or deploy-frozen host wants. None (the default) takes GENAI_OFFLINE from the environment; passing the argument overrides it.

    		 None

    Allow the repository's own Python to run at load time. Required by some architectures, and it executes code you did not review, so it stays opt-in.

    		 False
    idle_unload_seconds float | None

    When set, :meth:unload_if_idle frees the model after this many idle seconds.

    		 None
    hardware HardwareInfo | None

    Injected snapshot for device resolution (tests); probed when None.

    		 None
    generation_cache GenerationCache | AsyncGenerationCache | None

    Optional prompt→completion cache. Only deterministic generations (do_sample=False / temperature=0) are cached; sampling calls always run the model.

    		 None
    metrics GenAIMetrics | None

    Optional Prometheus metrics; when set, generate / chat record request count and latency (op "generate" / "chat").

    		 None
    config GenerationConfig | None

    Default generation parameters for every call. A call's own config is layered over it field by field, and its keyword overrides win over both. This is how a caller that passes no options — the :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.agents.Agent loop — still gets a bounded max_new_tokens or greedy decoding.

    		 None
    max_concurrent int | None

    Decodings this instance runs at once; the rest wait their turn, in arrival order. None (the default) starts every call immediately, each on its own worker thread. On CPU, set 1: one decode already uses every intra-op thread, so concurrent calls only split the cores. Measured with Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, four concurrent calls, 128 forced tokens: 22.4 tokens/s and a 22.73 s median latency with no limit, 26.9 tokens/s and 11.91 s with 1. The default stays None because the gain was measured on CPU only. Decoding runs on a pool of this many threads owned by the generator, never on the loop's default executor: torch's OpenMP keeps one worker team per calling thread, and a semaphore over the shared executor measured 18.5 tokens/s on the same load, slower than no limit at all. Process-wide thread count is torch's (torch.set_num_threads) and is deliberately not a knob here.

    chat_structured async ¶

    messages: list[dict[str, Any]],

    Generate a chat reply constrained to a Pydantic schema.

    The same call :meth:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.ollama.OllamaGenerator.chat_structured answers, so a service that reads documents into schemas runs on a local model or on a daemon without a line changing at the call site — see :class:StructuredTextBackend. The turns matter: concatenating a long instruction ahead of a long document makes a model start answering with the document, while the same instruction in its own system turn is respected. Sharing that contract across backends is what makes the two swappable in practice rather than only in type.

    Where the two differ is how the schema is enforced. The daemon takes a JSON schema and constrains decoding itself; here the constraint is a lm-format-enforcer token filter ([genai-structured] extra), and both paths end in the same :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.structured.parse_structured.

    Generate a completion for prompt.

    Runs the blocking model in a worker thread so the event loop stays free. A thread cannot be interrupted, so cancelling the coroutine that awaits this (a timeout, a client that went away) sets the stop event the model checks after every token — the caller's stop_event when one was passed — and decoding ends within one token instead of running to max_new_tokens for nobody.

    load ¶

    load() -> None

    Download (if needed) and load the model + tokenizer into memory.

    Idempotent — a no-op once loaded. Called automatically by :meth:generate / :meth:stream / :meth:chat. Safe to call from several threads at once: concurrent callers on a cold instance wait for one build instead of each running from_pretrained. It blocks for the whole download and build, so call it through asyncio.to_thread from async code.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ImportError

    When the [genai] (or [genai-quant]) extra is missing.

    stream async ¶

    stream(
    prompt: str, *, config: GenerationConfig | None = None, **kwargs: Any
) -> AsyncIterator[str]

    Stream the completion token by token.

    The generation runs on a worker thread and hands each piece to the event loop through call_soon_threadsafe, so the loop never blocks — not on the first-call load, not while waiting for the next token. Closing the iterator early (a client disconnecting, a break, aclose()) sets an internal stop event that the model checks after every token, so decoding stops within one token instead of running to max_new_tokens for nobody; the close itself returns without waiting for the worker thread.

    Measured with Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER: the first (cold) stream used to stall the loop for 4190 ms while the weights loaded on it, now 164 to 193 ms over three runs; closing after 5 of 200 tokens used to block for 3532 ms, now about 0.01 ms, with the worker thread done 28 ms later.

    With max_concurrent set, the stream holds one of the pool's workers from its first token until that thread returns — after the last token, or one token after the iterator was closed. A stream closed while still queued is dropped from the queue and never runs.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    prompt str

    The input text.

    		 required
    config GenerationConfig | None

    Typed generation parameters.

    		 None
    **kwargs Any

    Generation overrides (win over config).

    		 {}

    Yields:

    Name Type Description
    str AsyncIterator[str]

    Text pieces as they are produced.

    unload ¶

    unload() -> None

    Free the model and its memory (VRAM/RAM).

    Safe to call when not loaded. After this, the next generation call reloads the weights. While generations are in flight the release waits for them: the last one to finish drops the weights, so a running call never has its model freed underneath it.

    unload_if_idle ¶

    unload_if_idle() -> bool

    Unload the model when it has been idle past the threshold.

    Call periodically (e.g. from a @tq.interval task) to reclaim VRAM between bursts. A no-op when idle_unload_seconds is unset, the model isn't loaded, a generation is in flight, or it isn't idle enough yet.

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    bool bool

    True when it unloaded, False otherwise.

    TokenUsage dataclass ¶

    TokenUsage(
    input_tokens: int = 0,
    output_tokens: int = 0,
    total_tokens: int = 0,
    cache_hit_tokens: int = 0,
    cache_write_tokens: int = 0,
)

    What one generation call consumed, as the provider reported it.

    total is carried rather than recomputed from the two halves. Every provider is free to bill something other than input + output — cached-prefix discounts and reasoning tokens both show up that way — so the reported total is the authority, and :meth:from_payload only falls back to the sum when the field is absent.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    input_tokens int

    Tokens in the prompt.
    output_tokens int

    Tokens generated.
    total_tokens int

    What the provider counts for the call.
    cache_hit_tokens int

    The slice of input_tokens the provider served from a cached prefix and billed at a reduced rate — not tokens on top of the prompt. Adding it to input_tokens double-counts. 0 when the provider reported none, which is also what a provider that has no prompt cache reports.
    cache_write_tokens int

    The slice of input_tokens the provider wrote to its prompt cache on this call, billed at a premium on providers that charge for the write (Anthropic's cache_creation_input_tokens). Like cache_hit_tokens it is already counted in input_tokens. 0 on the OpenAI-compatible wire format, whose usage reports no write.

    from_payload classmethod ¶

    from_payload(payload: object) -> TokenUsage | None

    Build a usage from a provider's usage object.

    Reads the OpenAI-compatible spelling (prompt_tokens / completion_tokens / total_tokens), which DeepSeek, vLLM, TGI and the OpenAI API itself all emit.

    The cached-prefix count has two spellings in that same family, so both are read: DeepSeek's flat prompt_cache_hit_tokens and OpenAI's nested prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens. Reading only one of them silently prices a discounted call at full rate on the other provider, which is a wrong number rather than a missing one.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    payload object

    The usage object from the response, or None when the response carried none.

    		 required

    Returns:

    Type Description
    TokenUsage | None

    TokenUsage | None: The parsed usage, or None when payload
    TokenUsage | None

    is not a mapping — including when it is None. Callers treat
    TokenUsage | None

    that as "nothing to record", which is honest: a zeroed usage
    TokenUsage | None

    would claim the call was free.

    download_model ¶

    download_model(
    model_id: str,
    *,
    revision: str | None = None,
    cache_dir: str | None = None,
    token: str | None = None,
    local_files_only: bool | None = None,
    allow_patterns: list[str] | None = None,
    ignore_patterns: list[str] | None = None,
    check_disk: bool = True,
    disk_margin: float = 1.1,
) -> ModelSnapshot

    Materialize a model's weights on local disk, ahead of first use.

    Left to itself, the first /generate request pays for a multi-gigabyte download inside the request. Call this from the image build, the deploy step or a warm-up task instead, and the request path only ever loads from disk.

    check_disk refuses to start a download the filesystem cannot hold. Failing in two seconds with a number beats failing forty minutes later with a half-written cache. The estimate counts only the files allow_patterns / ignore_patterns select (filtered by the same huggingface_hub function snapshot_download uses) and leaves out the ones already in the cache for that revision.

    Example:

    >>> snapshot = download_model(
...     "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
...     revision="main",
...     allow_patterns=["*.json", "*.safetensors"],
... )
>>> snapshot.size_bytes > 0
True

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model_id str

    The Hub model id.

    		 required
    revision str | None

    Branch, tag or sha; None for the Hub default.

    		 None
    cache_dir str | None

    Where to write; None uses the HF_HUB_CACHE default.

    		 None
    token str | None

    Token for gated or private repositories.

    		 None
    local_files_only bool

    Resolve from the cache without touching the network (turns this call into a "is it already here?" check).

    		 None
    allow_patterns list[str] | None

    Only fetch files matching these globs — e.g. skip the .bin duplicates of a repo that also ships .safetensors.

    		 None
    ignore_patterns list[str] | None

    Skip files matching these globs.

    		 None
    check_disk bool

    Verify free space before downloading — the bytes of the selected files that are not cached yet.

    		 True
    disk_margin float

    Multiplier applied to the estimated size for the free-space check. The default 1.1 covers the temporary files the download writes next to the blobs.

    		 1.1

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    ModelSnapshot ModelSnapshot

    Where the weights landed, how big they are and
    ModelSnapshot

    how many files they span.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ImportError

    When huggingface_hub is not installed.
    OSError

    When check_disk is on and the target filesystem has less free space than the estimate times disk_margin.

    extract_json_list ¶

    extract_json_list(text: str) -> list[Any] | None

    Pull a JSON array out of a model completion, without raising.

    A prompt asking for "a list of items" comes back as an array, and the ways it arrives malformed differ from an object: a fence the prompt asked the model not to add, a sentence before the payload, one stray ] at the end. This tolerates all three.

    Returning None instead of raising is the point: it is the signal to retry the generation, which is a different response from "the model answered, and the answer was an empty list". A caller that cannot tell those apart either retries a valid empty result or gives up on a recoverable formatting slip.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    text str

    The raw model completion.

    		 required

    Returns:

    Type Description
    list[Any] | None

    list[Any] | None: The decoded list, or None when the completion
    list[Any] | None

    holds no decodable array (no array at all, malformed JSON, or a valid
    list[Any] | None

    JSON value that is not a list).

    Example:

    >>> extract_json_list('Here you go:\n```json\n[{"a": 1}]\n```')
[{'a': 1}]
>>> extract_json_list("not a list") is None
True

    extract_json_object ¶

    extract_json_object(text: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None

    Pull a JSON object out of a model completion, without raising.

    The object-shaped twin of :func:extract_json_list, for the prompt whose answer is one record rather than a list — an intent classifier, a routing decision, an extraction with fixed fields.

    :func:parse_structured already handles that shape, but it raises, which is the wrong contract when the caller's answer to bad output is "generate again" rather than "fail the request". Returning None says "retry" in one value, with no exception to catch and re-raise around a retry loop.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    text str

    The raw model completion.

    		 required

    Returns:

    Type Description
    dict[str, Any] | None

    dict[str, Any] | None: The decoded object, or None when the
    dict[str, Any] | None

    completion holds no decodable object (none at all, malformed JSON,
    dict[str, Any] | None

    or a valid JSON value that is not an object — a bare list included).

    Example:

    >>> extract_json_object('```json\n{"intent": "create_task"}\n```')
{'intent': 'create_task'}
>>> extract_json_object("[1, 2]") is None
True

    generate_structured_list async ¶

    generate_structured_list(
    backend: SupportsGenerate,
    prompt: str,
    schema: type[StructuredT],
    *,
    config: GenerationConfig | None = None,
    max_attempts: int = 3,
    temperature_step: float = 0.2,
    skip_invalid: bool = True,
) -> list[StructuredT]

    Generate a list of schema items, retrying on unusable output.

    Retrying a failed generation at the same temperature is close to pointless: greedy decoding is deterministic, so attempt two reproduces attempt one. Each retry therefore adds temperature_step, giving sampling a real chance to leave the bad state. The first attempt stays greedy, because it is the most reliable one.

    Only a structural failure costs an attempt — no array in the output at all. An array that parses but holds one malformed item is not a formatting failure, so it is handled by skip_invalid rather than by burning a generation.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    backend SupportsGenerate

    Anything with async generate(prompt, *, config=...) -> str — the local TextGenerator, OllamaGenerator, or OpenAICompatGenerator.

    		 required
    prompt str

    The prompt, which should ask for a JSON array.

    		 required
    schema type[StructuredT]

    The Pydantic model each item must match.

    		 required
    config GenerationConfig | None

    Base parameters. Its temperature is replaced per attempt; everything else is kept.

    		 None
    max_attempts int

    Generations to spend before giving up.

    		 3
    temperature_step float

    Added per retry (attempt 1 at 0.0, attempt 2 at temperature_step, and so on).

    		 0.2
    skip_invalid bool

    Drop items that fail validation instead of raising.

    		 True

    Returns:

    Type Description
    list[StructuredT]

    list[StructuredT]: The validated items. An **empty list is a
    list[StructuredT]

    success** — the model answered, and the answer is no items.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    StructuredFormatError

    No attempt produced a decodable array.
    ValueError

    When max_attempts is below 1.
    ValidationError

    When an item fails validation and skip_invalid is False.

    hosted_generator ¶

    hosted_generator(
    model: str,
    *,
    api_key: str,
    provider: HostedProvider | None = None,
    base_url: str | None = None,
    timeout: float = 120.0,
    retry_policy: RetryPolicy | None = None,
    http_client: HTTPClient | None = None,
    transport: AsyncBaseTransport | None = None,
) -> AnthropicGenerator | OpenAICompatGenerator

    Build the hosted generator for model.

    provider defaults to :func:resolve_provider; base_url defaults to the provider's documented root. On top of that, each provider gets the wire settings it documents:

    • anthropic — :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.AnthropicGenerator;
    • openai — the output budget as :data:OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS_FIELD and json_schema structured output;
    • google — :data:DEFAULT_GOOGLE_OPENAI_URL, json_schema structured output and :data:GOOGLE_EFFORT_VALUES;
    • deepseek — json_object structured output (the only JSON mode DeepSeek documents) and no reasoning_effort field.

    google and deepseek are also built with accepts_documents=False (see :func:supports_documents): a call carrying a :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.document_part raises ValueError before the request is sent.

    HostedGenAISettings.hosted_kwargs() returns exactly these keyword arguments, so building from settings is a splat.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model str

    The model id.

    		 required
    api_key str

    The provider's API key. Empty raises in the generator constructor.

    		 required
    provider HostedProvider | None

    The provider, when the model id does not say it.

    		 None
    base_url str | None

    API root, for a proxy or a regional endpoint.

    		 None
    timeout float

    Per-request HTTP timeout in seconds.

    		 120.0
    retry_policy RetryPolicy | None

    Retry configuration for the lazily-created HTTP client.

    		 None
    http_client HTTPClient | None

    An injected client for connection reuse.

    		 None
    transport AsyncBaseTransport | None

    Transport for the lazily-created client — an httpx.MockTransport in tests.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Type Description
    AnthropicGenerator | OpenAICompatGenerator

    AnthropicGenerator | OpenAICompatGenerator: The generator.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    When the provider cannot be resolved, provider is not one of :data:HOSTED_PROVIDERS (a string from configuration is not checked by the type), or api_key is empty.
    Example

    gen = hosted_generator("claude-haiku-5-5", api_key="sk-ant-...") isinstance(gen, AnthropicGenerator) True
