    make_ai_chat_router ¶

    make_ai_chat_router(
    pipeline: AIChatPipeline,
    *,
    prefix: str = "/api/ai-chat",
    tags: list[str] | None = None,
    current_user_id: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    dependencies: Sequence[Any] | None = None,
    docs_locale: str | None = None,
) -> APIRouter

    Mount an :class:AIChatPipeline on HTTP endpoints.

    Registers two endpoints:

    • POST {prefix}/chat — a full turn returning an :class:AIChatResult (reply, sources, memory hits, tool names, optional audio).
    • POST {prefix}/chat/stream — the reply streamed token-by-token over SSE, ending with a done event.

    The router is stateless: history rides in on each request body and the caller persists it however they like (see the module docstring on why the chat/ domain is intentionally not wired). The body is untrusted: history roles are limited to user/assistant, and the conversation owner — the key memory is recalled and indexed under — comes from current_user_id, never from the body.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    pipeline AIChatPipeline

    The configured pipeline to expose.

    		 required
    prefix str

    URL prefix. Defaults to "/api/ai-chat".

    		 '/api/ai-chat'
    tags list[str] | None

    OpenAPI tags. Defaults to ["ai-chat"].

    		 None
    current_user_id Callable[..., Any] | None

    FastAPI dependency resolving the authenticated caller's user id. Required when the pipeline has a memory: recalling under an id taken from the request would hand one user's past messages to anyone who names them. Without it, turns run with no memory owner.

    		 None
    dependencies Sequence[Any] | None

    Applied to every route — where authentication and rate limiting go.

    		 None
    docs_locale str | None

    Language of the OpenAPI summary and description text — "en-US" or "pt-BR". None (default) reads API_DOCS_LOCALE through :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.settings.ServerSettings, whose default is "en-US".

    		 None

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    APIRouter APIRouter

    Ready to mount with app.include_router.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    When the pipeline has a memory and no current_user_id was given.

    make_genai_router ¶

    make_genai_router(
    *,
    text_generator: TextBackend | None = None,
    embedder: SupportsEmbed | None = None,
    retriever: SupportsRetrieve | None = None,
    speech_to_text: SpeechTranscriber | None = None,
    text_to_speech: SpeechSynthesizer | None = None,
    image_generator: ImageGenerator | None = None,
    audio_generator: SupportsAudioGeneration | None = None,
    models: ModelRegistry | dict[str, Any] | list[Any] | None = None,
    prefix: str = "/api/genai",
    tags: list[str] | None = None,
    limits: GenAIRequestLimits | None = None,
    docs_locale: str | None = None,
) -> APIRouter

    Build a router exposing whichever GenAI objects you inject.

    Only the endpoints backed by a provided object are registered:

    • text_generator -> POST {prefix}/generate (JSON reply) and POST {prefix}/generate/stream (token-by-token SSE), plus POST {prefix}/chat.
    • embedder -> POST {prefix}/embed.
    • retriever -> POST {prefix}/rag (query -> context block).
    • speech_to_text -> POST {prefix}/transcribe (audio upload).
    • text_to_speech -> POST {prefix}/tts (returns audio/wav).
    • image_generator -> POST {prefix}/image (returns the encoded image, with the seed in X-Image-Seed).
    • audio_generator -> POST {prefix}/audio (returns one audio/wav clip, with the seed in X-Audio-Seed).
    • models -> GET {prefix}/models (what is resident in memory right now, next to the host's memory picture).

    The router owns only the HTTP surface; the caller owns model lifecycle (loading, idle-unloading, auth). Add your own auth by including the router under an authenticated parent or wrapping it.

    Every request is checked against limits before the model runs: prompt length, chat size, max_new_tokens, /embed batch size, top_k, /tts text length, image size and steps, and the /transcribe upload size (read in chunks, so an oversized upload is refused before it is held in memory). A request over any of them gets 422 -- except the upload, which gets 413 (UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE); with register_exception_handlers installed the body also carries details={"field": ..., "limit": ...} (or {"max_bytes": ...} for the upload). /image answers with one image, so it refuses config.num_images above 1 instead of rendering a batch and dropping all but the first.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    text_generator TextBackend | None

    Backs the text endpoints (a TextGenerator, an OllamaGenerator, or any object implementing the TextBackend protocol).

    		 None
    embedder SupportsEmbed | None

    Backs /embed (an Embedder, an OllamaEmbedder, or any SupportsEmbed).

    		 None
    retriever SupportsRetrieve | None

    Backs /rag — a Retriever (rerank via Retriever(reranker=...)) or a HybridRetriever.

    		 None
    speech_to_text SpeechTranscriber | None

    Backs /transcribe — a SpeechToText, an OpenAICompatSpeech, an OllamaSpeech, or any SpeechTranscriber. The route takes an optional prompt form field (checked against max_prompt_chars) and forwards it; temperature is not exposed.

    		 None
    text_to_speech SpeechSynthesizer | None

    Backs /tts — a TextToSpeech, an OllamaSpeech, or any SpeechSynthesizer.

    		 None
    image_generator ImageGenerator | None

    Backs /image.

    		 None
    audio_generator SupportsAudioGeneration | None

    Backs /audio -- an AudioGenerator, a MusicGenerator, or any SupportsAudioGeneration.

    		 None
    models ModelRegistry | dict[str, Any] | list[Any] | None

    Backs /models — a ModelRegistry, or a dict/list of handles you hold yourself.

    		 None
    prefix str

    URL prefix. Defaults to "/api/genai".

    		 '/api/genai'
    tags list[str] | None

    OpenAPI tags. Defaults to ["genai"].

    		 None
    limits GenAIRequestLimits | None

    Per-request ceilings. None uses GenAIRequestLimits() and its defaults.

    		 None
    docs_locale str | None

    Language of the OpenAPI summary and description text — "en-US" or "pt-BR". None (default) reads API_DOCS_LOCALE through :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.settings.ServerSettings, whose default is "en-US".

    		 None

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    APIRouter APIRouter

    Ready to mount with app.include_router.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    When no GenAI object is provided (the router would be empty). Emptiness is tested with is None, not truthiness: an empty ModelRegistry — the normal state at startup, before anything has been loaded — is falsy, and refusing it would make the endpoint impossible to mount at the only time you can mount it.

    make_generation_key ¶

    make_generation_key(
    model_id: str,
    prompt: str,
    params: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    operation: str = "generate",
    identity: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> str

    Build a stable cache key from the model, prompt and parameters.

    operation separates call shapes that share a prompt string: a chat keyed on the serialized messages must not answer a generate whose prompt happens to be that same JSON text. identity carries whatever else pins the weights behind model_id (revision, quantization), so two generators of the same model id loaded differently never read each other's completions.

    The default operation="generate" with no identity produces the same digest as before either argument existed, so an existing Redis cache of plain generate calls stays warm.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    model_id str

    The model identifier.

    		 required
    prompt str

    The input prompt (or serialized messages).

    		 required
    params dict[str, Any]

    Generation parameters that affect the output.

    		 required
    operation str

    The call shape ("generate", "chat" …).

    		 'generate'
    identity Mapping[str, Any] | None

    Extra model identity fields; entries whose value is None are ignored.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    str str

    A hex SHA-256 digest.

    Snapshot the host's CPU, RAM, GPU and disk.

    GPU name and memory come from NVML when pynvml is installed, so a web process that probes (the /models endpoint, a health check) does not create a CUDA context on every GPU. Without NVML it falls back to torch.cuda.mem_get_info, which does initialize CUDA in the calling process. has_cuda always comes from torch.cuda.is_available(), which does not create a context.

    recommend ¶

    recommend(
    *,
    num_params: int | None = None,
    model_id: str | None = None,
    hardware: HardwareInfo | None = None,
    token: str | None = None,
) -> CapacityReport

    Pick the best precision that fits, from the native one down to int4.

    Tries the precision TextGenerator(dtype="auto") loads on the auto-selected device (bfloat16 on CUDA/MPS, float32 on CPU), then int8, then int4, and returns the first :class:CapacityReport that fits (or the int4 report when nothing fits, so the caller sees the closest option). A report whose dtype is int8/int4 maps to TextGenerator(quantization=...); any other dtype is what dtype="auto" already loads.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    num_params int | None

    The model's parameter count.

    		 None
    model_id str | None

    Hub id to look the count up from.

    		 None
    hardware HardwareInfo | None

    Injected snapshot; defaults to a fresh probe.

    		 None
    token str | None

    Hub token for the lookup.

    		 None

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    CapacityReport CapacityReport

    The recommended configuration. When the free memory
    CapacityReport

    of the device could not be measured (memory_measured=False), it
    CapacityReport

    is the report at the native precision: the ladder needs a number to
    CapacityReport

    step down from, and stepping to int4 on an unknown would
    CapacityReport

    recommend a slower, lossier load for nothing.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    When neither num_params nor a resolvable model_id is available.
    Notes

    Two fallbacks are tried in order: a smaller precision on the same device first, since that keeps the model on the accelerator, and only then CPU RAM when the current device is a GPU.

    truncate_messages ¶

    truncate_messages(
    messages: list[dict[str, Any]],
    max_tokens: int,
    tokenizer: TokenEncoder,
    *,
    keep_system: bool = True,
    per_message_overhead: int = DEFAULT_PER_MESSAGE_OVERHEAD,
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]

    Drop the oldest turns until the chat fits within max_tokens.

    System messages are kept (when keep_system) and moved to the front; the most recent turn is always kept even if it alone exceeds the budget. The oldest non-system, non-last turns are dropped first.

    An assistant turn carrying tool_calls and the role="tool" results that answer it are dropped together, never split: a history that starts with a tool result whose call was trimmed away, or ends a call with no result, breaks the pairing the OpenAI chat format requires between a call and its results, and strict providers refuse it. If the most recent turn is such a tool result, its whole group (the call plus every result) is what is always kept.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    messages list[dict[str, Any]]

    The full chat history.

    		 required
    max_tokens int

    The token budget to fit within.

    		 required
    tokenizer TokenEncoder

    Tokenizer exposing encode.

    		 required
    keep_system bool

    Always retain system messages.

    		 True
    per_message_overhead int

    Per-message overhead used in the estimate.

    		 DEFAULT_PER_MESSAGE_OVERHEAD

    Returns:

    Type Description
    list[dict[str, Any]]

    list[dict[str, Any]]: The trimmed messages (system first, then the kept
    list[dict[str, Any]]

    tail in order). Empty input returns an empty list.
